topic: Your brain's best guess 3: Strangers enjoy talking more than you predict
caption:
Strangers enjoy talking more than you predict.

The prediction: chatting to a stranger probably won’t go well.

Across several studies, conversations with strangers tended to go better than people predicted beforehand. Worries about our own conversation skills, and about being rejected, seem to run ahead of what actually happens.

Something to try: You might say one friendly sentence to someone in a queue.

Your brain's best guess is our series on everyday predictions that research suggests are often too pessimistic. Studies were mostly with student and online samples, so results may differ for you.

Research: Sandstrom, G. M., & Boothby, E. J. (2021). Why do people avoid talking to strangers? A mini meta-analysis of predicted fears and actual experiences talking to a stranger. Self and Identity, 20(1), 47-71. https://doi.org/10.1080/15298868.2020.1816568
